# Cartan-power completion of the full rank-two projection problem

This is the strongest live auxiliary object from the continuation. It does not decide the all-copy inequality. It uses an established coherent-state approximation theorem; neither that theorem nor the general coherent-state hierarchy method is claimed as invented here. The application, constants, and explicit opposition are given completely below.

## 1. The object, without an unknown positivity premise

Let H=(C^3)^{tensor n}, D=3^n. A unit decomposable bivector

\[
z=u\wedge v=(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)/\sqrt2,
\qquad u\perp v,\quad\|u\|=\|v\|=1,
\]

has one-replica marginal P/2, where P=uu*+vv* is a rank-two projection. Define the **Cartan power**

\[
\mathcal C_k(H)=\operatorname{span}\{z^{\otimes k}:z\text{ decomposable}\}
\subset\operatorname{Sym}^k(\wedge^2H),\qquad k\ge2.
\]

This is the irreducible U(D) representation with highest weight (k,k). It is constructible by the rectangular two-row Young symmetrizer: antisymmetrize each of the k columns and symmetrize the two rows, taking the corresponding image. Thus defining the space does not require a solution of Werner positivity. Its dimension is

\[
d_D(k)=\frac{(D+k-1)!(D+k-2)!}
{(D-1)!(D-2)!\,k!\,(k+1)!}.\tag{1}
\]

Grouping the first two bivector columns gives the canonical inclusion

\[
\mathcal C_k(H)\subset\mathcal C_2(H)\otimes\mathcal C_{k-2}(H).
\]

For k=2 the second factor is scalar. This inclusion is already evident on the spanning coherent powers, and is the highest-weight-sum inclusion needed by the cited approximation theorem.

Each bivector column consists of two H replicas, called a,b in the first column and c,d in the second. Let

\[
B_n=A_n^{(a,c)}\otimes I_{b,d},
\qquad A_n=\prod_{i=1}^n(F_{ac,i}-I/2).
\]

For R a density matrix on \(\mathcal C_k(H)\), let R^(2) be its first two-column marginal and set

\[
\alpha_{n,k}=\min_R\operatorname{Tr}(R^{(2)}B_n).\tag{2}
\]

This is a finite smallest-eigenvalue/PSD problem on an explicit linear representation space. For a coherent density matrix \(|z\rangle\langle z|^{\otimes k}\), tracing b,d gives (P/2) tensor (P/2), so the value is q_n(P)/4. Every rank-two projection occurs. In particular

\[
\alpha_{n,k}\le g_n/4.\tag{3}
\]

\qquad q_n(C)=b_n(C,C).
\]

either the full target holds and every \(g_n=0\), or it fails and \(\limsup_n g_n<0\). These prior results are used at their actual scope; the projection reduction and gap dichotomy are not new results of this continuation.

# Independent mathematical review of L42 and L67

**Verdict.** Both continuations contain correct substantive auxiliary mathematics at their stated scopes. Neither proves the all-copy qutrit inequality, supplies a negative admissible rank-two witness, or improves the initial upper bound on the Cauchy growth invariant. L42 constructs explicit convergent full-domain relaxations and proves a consequential all-finite-degree obstruction. L67 solves a quantitative one-copy certificate-cone problem and extends its obstruction uniformly in copy number. These are different contributions; neither is foundational completion.

**Exposure.** I read the common task, source references, initial endpoint, both assigned endpoints, the complete supplied N525 proof, relevant common-source passages, and primary literature listed below. The endpoint headings explicitly say “Fresh continuation result” (L42) and “Warm-continuation result” / “Warm continuation handoff” (L67). L42 also refers to “Frozen B first-stage.” Thus this was **not blind to the fresh/warm distinction**. I did not inspect the experimental protocol, hypotheses, assignment key, other pair, private programme files, or live researcher folders. Pinned-repository access consisted only of `git show` for N525's shadow-LP source and receipt.

## L42: accepted global objects and obstruction, with the asymptotic bound still missing

The Cartan space is a constructed representation, not a definition requiring unknown Werner positivity. Its coherent vectors correspond to every complex two-plane; their one-replica marginals are \(P/2\). The canonical highest-weight inclusion into degrees \(2\) and \(k-2\) is the inclusion required by [Christandl–König–Mitchison–Renner, Theorem II.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0602130v4). The paper uses half the full trace norm. Consequently the endpoint's full-norm error \(4(1-d_D(k-2)/d_D(k))\), rather than half that amount, is correct. \]
